rework_history: The runtime adapter's first candidate proved that RootPermit-v1 bound only the pre-decision action and target, so a caller could substitute the complete effect resolution while retaining the same permit.
RootPermit-v2 separates action-only Resume and Recover issuance from Reconcile issuance and binds Reconcile to a domain-separated commitment over the complete typed EffectResolution.

root_integration.root_dependency_result: 42 passed; 0 failed; one non-reproduced leak diagnostic

closed_findings: RootPermit-v1 schema and domain are rejected and missing decision bindings cannot deserialize.
Resume and Recover accept only action-bound permits while Reconcile accepts only an exact resolution-bound permit.
The resolution commitment covers operation identity, evidence digest, outcome, and every applied receipt field.
Resolution shape and exact permit decision binding are verified before the durable workspace can mutate.
Root actor, context and candidate binding, workspace identity, expected journal head, operation, target, expiry, nonce, and exact decision all participate in permit authentication.
Competing differently bound reconciliation decisions retain expected-head one-winner semantics and replay refusal.
Debug and serialized surfaces do not expose the root authority secret.

root_acceptance_limit: Production-compiled source-local RootPermit-v2 schema, exact action-versus-decision issuance interfaces, full EffectResolution commitment, and mutation-path verification behavior.
